clue.text: I'm so startled when confounded by a poser

indicators.note: confounded means thrown into confusion, so the letters of the opening words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone is taken aback on meeting a baffling puzzle or person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confounded' scrambles the twelve letters of I'M SO STARTLED. 'a poser' looks like a puzzle but is someone who poses for a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: A poser is one who sits still for a painter, the sitter hired by artists.

clue.text: Get Bill twenty-four sheets

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
a quire is a measure of paper, twenty-four (or twenty-five) sheets

explanation.surface: An instruction to buy a bundle of paper with some money.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to obtain or come to possess it.

clue.text: Neat road-junction on the border

parts.note: a T-junction is a road junction shaped like the letter T
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: A tidy crossroads lies along a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: Neat and tidy are synonyms for something kept in good order.

clue.text: Clean son followed by a tiny young dog

parts.note: wee is Scottish for tiny
a pup is a young dog

explanation.surface: A boy tidies up while trailed by a little puppy.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean a room you may gather the dirt with a broom, a phrasal verb of tidying.

clue.text: Acts in a fashion which is quite evil

indicators.note: in a fashion means made in a new way, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone behaves in a manner that is truly wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' rearranges ACTS IN A; the 'in a' of 'in a fashion' is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Something devilish, like the work of the Devil himself, is thoroughly wicked.

clue.text: Pair heartened by American greeting in America

indicators.note: heartened by means given a heart, so the greeting goes into the middle of the pair

parts.note: in cricket a pair is two ducks, scores of nought, written O and O
hi is an informal greeting, especially in America

explanation.surface: Two people are cheered by a friendly hello in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a 'pair' is being out for nought in both innings, so two Os.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition is loose: the answer is a Midwestern state located in the USA.

clue.text: Sovereign has to set out the argument

annotationWithheld.why: Sovereign has to set out the argument (7): POUND comes from 'Sovereign' but no clue word gives EX; a word such as 'Former' looks lost in OCR.
annotationWithheld.clue: Sovereign has to set out the argument

clue.text: Reprimanded for having one's writings published

definitions.meaning: called to account and made to answer for one's conduct
read literally, one's writing made into a bound volume

explanation.surface: An author is scolded for getting into print.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means made to answer for misdeeds; literally it would mean put into a bound volume.

clue.text: Marvellous subject for The Racing News'

parts.note: grand means splendid or marvellous
a national is a citizen or subject of a country

explanation.surface: A great story for a horse-racing paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's famous steeplechase run at Aintree each spring, always headline racing news.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known steeplechase in Britain fills the horse-racing pages every year.

clue.text: Army men truly needed to get satisfaction

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of army men
quite can mean truly or entirely

explanation.surface: Soldiers who are honest are required to achieve contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is the Royal Engineers, a regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: To repay a wrong or a kindness in kind is to take satisfaction for it.

clue.text: Tourist who is heading fora fall

definitions.meaning: a day visitor on an outing
read literally, one who stumbles and is about to fall over

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker is riding for a tumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A day visitor on an excursion is one sense; literally, one who stumbles is the other.

clue.text: One upper-class fool suffering a setback

parts.note: a nit is a silly person, a fool

explanation.surface: A posh idiot meets with a reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering a setback' has no job in the wordplay: U and NIT already give the answer in order, so it is surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A single item, one of a whole, is a single thing counted on its own.

clue.text: Exhausted writer getting in the way

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the writer is placed inside the road

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A tired author is obstructing traffic.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent and worn out both describe energy that has been used up.

clue.text: One put in to organise a tumbledown house

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so the numeral goes inside the verb

parts.note: to run something is to organise or manage it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A person is installed to manage a dilapidated home.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreck of a building, falling down from decay, is a ruined structure.

clue.text: What the Palestinians most want to say

definitions.meaning: a nation with its own government, sovereign nationhood
to declare or put into words

explanation.surface: A remark about Palestinian aspirations and the right to speak.
explanation.definitionFit: A sovereign country is one sense; to declare or express is the other.

clue.text: Rings up small bear of very little brain

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the bear's name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Winnie-the-Pooh calls himself a bear of very little brain

explanation.surface: Someone telephones a little dim-witted teddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns POOH into HOOP. Pooh, A. A. Milne's teddy bear, describes himself as a Bear of Very Little Brain.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoops are circular bands, so they are circles or rings.

clue.text: Last of the wine put down by Fred Astaire?

definitions.meaning: the dregs left in the bottom of a glass
read literally, a tap struck with the back of the foot in a dance

explanation.surface: A famous dancer sets down the dregs of his drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Astaire was a celebrated tap dancer.
explanation.definitionFit: The dregs left in a glass are one sense; a tap-dancer's beat with the back of the shoe is the other.

clue.text: Runs into demure fellow south of London

indicators.note: into means going inside, so the runs are placed within the shy word

parts.note: coy means shy or demure
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a don is a fellow of a college

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into a modest man on the city's southern edge.
explanation.walkthrough: CROYDON is a large town in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: The borough lies in the southern suburbs of the capital.

clue.text: Characteristic otherwise displayed by Judas

parts.note: a trait is a characteristic
or means otherwise, as in hurry or else

explanation.surface: A feature that Judas showed in another way.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas Iscariot betrayed Jesus, so his name stands for a betrayer.

clue.text: He sounds like a vinegary old stylite

indicators.note: sounds like means the word for vinegary is said and heard as another word

parts.note: acetic means of or like vinegar

explanation.surface: A sour-sounding hermit perched atop a pillar.
explanation.walkthrough: Stylites were early Christian hermits who lived on top of pillars.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylite lived on a pillar in extreme self-denial, a hermit of austere habits.

clue.text: Revised article for public reading

indicators.note: revised means altered, so the letters of the word are reorganised

explanation.surface: An edited piece of writing for reading out to an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: A performance of poetry or prose to an audience is a public reading.

clue.text: Plagiarist has advertising material to catalogue

parts.note: copy is the text of an advert
cat is short for catalogue

explanation.surface: A thief of words has some adverts for a brochure.
explanation.definitionFit: A plagiarist imitates others' work, as a mimic does.

clue.text: Conflicts caused by Conservative whips

parts.note: lashes are strokes of a whip, or as a verb, whips

explanation.surface: Disputes provoked by a Tory party's whips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whips' suggests party enforcers in Parliament, but here it is the verb or the strokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Clashes are fights or disputes, the same as conflicts.

clue.text: Staff College needs to accommodate one

indicators.note: to accommodate means to take in, so the number goes inside the college

parts.note: COLL is the abbreviation for college

explanation.surface: A military staff college must find room for a cadet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff College' reads as one institution, but 'Staff' is the definition, a staff officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior army officer is a member of the military staff.

clue.text: Composer dear to the Welsh

definitions.meaning: Johann Sebastian, the German Baroque composer
a Welsh term of endearment, like love or dear

explanation.surface: A musician beloved in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Johann Sebastian is the composer; in Wales the same word is a fond address.

clue.text: A little bit of a fight

explanation.surface: Something small from a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragment and a scuffle share this one word.

clue.text: Nothing after 151 is representative of history

parts.note: CLI is 151 in Roman numerals
O is nought, nothing

explanation.surface: A zero after a number stands for the past.
explanation.walkthrough: CLIO is the Muse of history in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muse who presides over history is its emblem.

clue.text: Large car for the Holy Roman Emperor in 1500

definitions.meaning: the Austin ..., a British family car
Maximilian I ruled the Empire in 1500

explanation.surface: A big automobile fit for an emperor of the year 1500.
explanation.walkthrough: The Austin Maxi was a British family car of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: A large British car model and the shortened name of Emperor Maximilian the First.

clue.text: Being written in palindromic form

indicators.note: written in palindromic form means the word reads the same both ways

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An existence spelt the same backwards and forwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin word for 'to be' reads the same in both directions.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy the Latin term means existence or essential nature.

clue.text: What the final batsman is given to survive

definitions.text: What the final batsman is given
definitions.meaning: the last batter dismissed is given ...

explanation.surface: The fate of the last cricketer at the crease.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the final batsman out is out last.
explanation.definitionFit: Live longer than another is to survive; in cricket the final dismissal is the other sense.

clue.text: High Priest returns to the house to give praise to God

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house

indicators.note: returns means goes back, so the priest's name is read backwards

parts.note: Annas was a Jewish high priest in the Gospels

explanation.surface: A senior cleric comes back home to give thanks to the Lord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns ANNAS into SANNA. Annas was high priest before Caiaphas at Jesus's trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The Palm Sunday cry is a shout of adoration in worship.

clue.text: The hit of Paris!

parts.note: not a song popular in the French capital: the Trojan prince Paris struck Achilles with an arrow in his one weak spot

explanation.surface: A celebration of a smash success in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Paris looks like the city, but it is the Trojan prince who shot Achilles in the heel.
explanation.definitionFit: The only place the Greek hero was vulnerable, where Paris's arrow struck, now means any weak point.
